- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent history, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for bullish momentum.  
- If model shows gradual upward trend but true outcome spikes sharply, model is lagging; adjust forecast to accelerate slope by 0.5–1.5% per day after spike.  
- If model forecast is flat or slightly declining while true outcome rises >5% from recent low, model is missing breakout; add 2–5% upward bias for next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment is neutral or negative (0.0), model often overpredicts; reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overconfidence bias.  
- If model forecast is consistently below true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, apply mean reversion correction: add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to align with recent upward trend.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds model by >10% in first 5 days, assume momentum is accelerating; apply 1–2% daily ramp-up to forecast.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.2 spikes, model tends to overshoot; cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak to avoid overcorrection.
